## TL;DR

The task panel's status card now derives its live-state heading from the same
helpers the board card uses instead of keeping a second hand-written copy. In
the reported scenario both surfaces read `running checks` while a handoff gate
runs, the panel shows the Settings-selected activity animation, and the block
is compact: blank rows and rows that merely repeat another row are removed.
Confirming handoff is capped at two lines (heading plus the current step), and
the Move-to-done pill and the status dropdown now use shared board-card copy and
the current status label. Targeted component tests cover checks running,
confirming handoff, and the integrating pill.

## Work and rationale

The root cause was duplicated state naming. `TaskCard.vue` resolves its label
through a long priority chain (`handoffInFlight`, `reviewFor().running`,
`activeEngineerCardHint`, integration pipeline copy, and so on), while
`TaskDrawer.vue` built a separate fixed tuple of strings in
`drawerStatusSummary`. The drawer's `confirmingHandoff` branch emitted three
rows — "Confirming handoff", "Handoff", "Running checks…" — even though the card
said `running checks` with an animated indicator.

I introduced `src/ui-app/src/lib/task-status-copy.ts` for the labels that both
surfaces must agree on: `running checks` (with the `· slow` suffix),
`awaiting fresh review`, `Reviewing…`, `PM is working`, and `Starting…`.
`TaskCard.vue` now imports those constants, so renaming a label on one surface
would fail to compile on the other rather than silently drifting.

For the panel I reused the card's actual resolvers rather than copying their
output text. `cardWorkHint` in the drawer runs the same `autoRepairHint` then
`activeEngineerCardHint` sequence as `codingOrStuckHint`. `cardChecksHeading`
resolves local queue, handoff gate, integration pipeline, and live-work labels
using `handoffInFlight`, `remotePoolQueueHintForTaskChecks`,
`integrationActiveCopy`, `integrationQueuedCopy`, and
`integrationProgressCardLabel`. That means a check running mid-work reads the
card's `checking · Step 4 of 8 · 2m` style label, while a handoff gate reads
`running checks`, exactly matching the card at that moment.

The drawer status model changed from a fixed three-string tuple to a filtered
`string[]`. A small `compactStatusLines` helper trims blanks and drops
case-insensitive duplicates of the heading or an earlier row. The template now
renders the heading plus a `v-for` over the rest, so empty rows cannot occupy
space; the CSS switched from a three-row grid to a flex column. Confirming
handoff therefore renders at most the shared heading and the live handoff step.
Reviewer running, which previously repeated itself with "Reviewer running /
Review / Reviewer is working…", now renders just `Reviewing…`, the card's own
label.

Running states now render the shared `ActivityIndicator` instead of the old
static pulsing dot. Checks, confirming handoff, and reviewer states use the
reviewing motion; work states use the coding motion; a PM-only run uses the
agent motion. That makes the panel honour `activityAnimationStyle` and
`activityAnimationSize` the same way the card does. The now-dead dot keyframes
were removed.

I also addressed the "More examples" acceptance addition. The Move-to-done pill
now prints `integrationCardLabel`, built from `integrationActiveCopy` /
`integrationQueuedCopy` / `integrationProgressCardLabel`, instead of its own
`Integrating… (stage · clock)` format. That gives integrating, queued, and
validating states one shared label and elapsed-time source between card and
panel. The status dropdown now renders a computed `currentStatusLabel` as both
its value text and placeholder, so an unmounted selected item during close-out
can no longer leave the trigger blank.

## Approaches tried

I first considered extracting the card's entire `hint` computed into a shared
function. That would guarantee agreement for every state, but it would need a
large context object assembled identically in two components and would move
card-only concerns (pipeline recovery, held state, done-error suppression,
needs-input hinting) into the drawer. The risk of a subtle behaviour change was
higher than the benefit for this bug, whose visible failures were the four
running states plus the integrating pill. Reusing the existing helpers at the
branches that matter keeps one source of truth without relocating the whole
decision tree.

I also considered adding new drawer status keys for `integrating` and `queued`.
Instead, the checks-running heading delegates to the same integration helpers
when a check run is active, and the Move-to-done pill independently uses the
shared integration label. This keeps the existing priority model intact and
avoids changing status-details semantics.

For tests, I mounted `TaskCard` and `TaskDrawer` against the same Pinia store in
one file and compared the card hint text with the panel heading directly. That
is a stronger guard than asserting an expected literal on each side, because it
will notice if either surface changes independently. I also kept the existing
drawer tests and updated their expectations to the new shared labels and compact
row counts.

## Challenges and blockers

The first targeted Vitest run failed because it used the root Vite config, which
does not load the Vue plugin; the repository's tests need
`--config src/ui-app/vite.config.ts`. Once run correctly, the new label-match
test passed, and the remaining failures were expected assertions from the old
three-line layout: the review-failed card no longer has a redundant "Review
report" row, the remote-work summary's static mark is now an indicator, and the
reviewer card no longer has a third "Reviewer is working…" row. Updating those
assertions matched the new acceptance criteria rather than hiding regressions.

`repoos check --changed main` passed all local steps (format, lint, build, CSS
and contrast guards, bare-require, UI smoke). It reported the test step as
skipped because the remote validation runner had already handled the suite. I
ran the affected component suites locally, and they pass. I did not independently
click through the managed preview; the declared shots for checks running and
confirming handoff are left for the handoff capture.

## Key learnings

Duplicated presentation copy is the real defect here, not just the wording. Two
components describing the same state eventually diverge because each one grows
its own special cases. The durable fix is to share the resolver, or at minimum
the label constants, and let tests compare the two rendered surfaces rather than
asserting literals twice.

Fixed-size status layouts also hide emptiness: a three-row grid looks fine when
every branch fills three strings, but it forces authors to invent filler rows.
Rendering only the lines that exist, and filtering repeats before rendering,
keeps the card honest and lets it shrink naturally. Finally, the status dropdown
blank was a reminder that a select value must not depend on the selected item
staying mounted; a computed text fallback is cheap and removes the whole class
of blank-trigger states.
